stemBlocks.value: (a) Calculate the values of x and y in the matrix equation (1  5 / 2  y)(-4  1 / 2  9) = (x  46 / 6  65). (b) A transformation T, represented by the matrix (0  1 / 1  0), maps S(2, 5) onto S'(5, 2). Describe fully the single transformation T.
Think first: Multiply out the left side entry by entry and match with the right side; each position gives its own equation.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p293-q04 from workbook page 293.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the top-left entry of the product.

contentBlocks.value: Result: Top-left = 6, and this equals x, so x = 6

solutionSteps.instruction: Check the top-right entry to confirm the multiplication.
Form an equation from the bottom-left entry.
For (b), see what the matrix does to a general point.

contentBlocks.value: (0  1 / 1  0)(x / y) = (y / x), and indeed S(2, 5) goes to (5, 2). Swapping the coordinates is reflection in y = x.
Result: T is a reflection in the line y = x

strategyBlocks.value: Work out each of the four entries of the product in terms of y, match them with the given matrix to find x and y, then interpret the effect of the matrix on coordinates for part (b).

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) x = 6 and y = 7.  (b) T is a reflection in the line y = x.

whyThisWorks.value: Two matrices are equal only when every corresponding pair of elements is equal, so a single matrix equation is really four ordinary equations at once, and you can pick whichever position gives the simplest one. A transformation matrix acts on the position vector of a point, so reading off its effect on a general column (x, y) identifies the transformation for every point at once, not just the one given.
